svg.title: Phase portrait: toroidalDipoleInit, meridional slice x₂ = ½
svg.desc: Contours of the azimuthal vorticity ω₂ of u₀ = curl A, A = h(x₃)(−s₂, s₁, 0), sᵢ = sin 2π(xᵢ − ½), h = sin 2πx₃ + κ sin 6πx₃, κ = 0.3, in the invariant plane x₂ = ½ of the unit cell Q = [0,1]³ (NavierStokesBlowup.lean, section H4). In this plane ω₂ = 8π² s₁ (sin 2πx₃ + 5κ sin 6πx₃).
svg.text: meridional slice x₂ = ½ of the unit cell Q = [0,1]³ · contours of the azimuthal vorticity ω₂ · κ = 0.3
u₀ = curl A, A = h(x₃)(−s₂, s₁, 0), h(x₃) = sin 2πx₃ + κ sin 6πx₃ (NavierStokesBlowup.lean, H4)

a.title: Observer Frame Boundary — click to inspect

g.text: Each closed family of contours, together with its mirror image across the axis, is the cross-section of one toroidal ring.
The pattern is odd across x₃ = ½ (mirror symmetry σ: x₃ ↦ −x₃, period 1), so the upper and lower rings rotate in opposite senses.
For κ > 0.2 (or κ < −1/15) a counter-rotating sub-layer appears inside each ring (here κ = 0.3); for κ = 0 each half-cell holds a single core.
Exactly what the Lean file proves about this datum: C^∞, periodic, divergence-free, mean zero, mirror-symmetric, non-zero for κ ≠ 1.
Nothing in the code proves that this datum blows up, or that it does not.
